title: Federated Personalization of Early-Exit Networks
abstract: arXiv:2601.10015v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Personalized Federated Learning (PFL) excels at tailoring client-specific models, which is particularly critical for decentralized and heterogeneous data environments, yet existing methods produce static models with a fixed tradeoff between accuracy and efficiency. This inherent static nature limits their ability to adapt to inference demands that vary with context and resource availability, posing a challenge for real-world deployment. Early-exit networks (EENs), which enable adaptive inference via intermediate classifiers, offer a promising solution. However, integrating EENs into PFL introduces two intertwined conflicts: client-wise heterogeneity across clients and depth-wise interference arising from conflicting exit objectives. Prior studies fail to resolve both conflicts simultaneously, leading to suboptimal performance. translated_title: 提前退出网络的联邦个性化
translated_abstract: 个性化联邦学习（PFL）擅长为客户端定制专属模型，这在去中心化和异构数据环境中尤为关键，然而现有方法产生的是静态模型，其精度与效率之间存在固定的权衡。这种固有的静态特性限制了模型适应随上下文和资源可用性而变化的推理需求的能力，为实际部署带来了挑战。提前退出网络（EENs）通过中间分类器实现自适应推理，为此提供了一种有前景的解决方案。然而，将EENs整合到PFL中会引入两个相互交织的冲突：客户端之间的异构性冲突，以及由退出目标相互冲突引起的深度干扰。先前的研究未能同时解决这两个冲突，导致性能欠佳。本文提出X-FED，一种新颖的冲突感知跨客户端联邦退出蒸馏框架。
tldr: 提出X-FED框架，通过冲突感知的跨客户端联邦退出蒸馏方法，同时解决个性化联邦学习中的客户端异构性与提前退出网络中的深度干扰两大冲突，实现精度与效率可自适应调节的个性化联邦学习。
en_tdlr: Proposes X-FED, a novel conflict-aware cross-client federated exit distillation framework that simultaneously resolves client-wise heterogeneity and depth-wise interference, enabling personalized federated learning with adaptive accuracy-efficiency tradeoffs via early-exit networks.
